original_query: SELECT t6.JOB, t8.NAME FROM (SELECT JOB, DEPTNO + EMPNO AS f9 FROM EMP WHERE ENAME = 'A' GROUP BY JOB, DEPTNO + EMPNO) AS t6 LEFT JOIN (SELECT NAME, DEPTNO + 5 AS f2 FROM DEPT GROUP BY NAME, DEPTNO + 5) AS t8 ON t6.JOB = t8.NAME AND t6.f9 = t8.f2 GROUP BY t6.JOB, t8.NAME
rewritten_query:
SELECT DISTINCT e.job, d.name
FROM emp e
LEFT JOIN dept d
  ON d.name = e.job
 AND d.deptno = (e.deptno + e.empno) - 5
WHERE e.ename = 'A';

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Both derived tables use GROUP BY on all selected columns with no aggregate functions; they are pure DISTINCT operations. The outer GROUP BY also only deduplicates final pairs. Replace all three grouping steps with a direct LEFT JOIN plus SELECT DISTINCT.

Rewrite the join predicate `d.deptno + 5 = e.deptno + e.empno` as `d.deptno = (e.deptno + e.empno) - 5`, isolating dept.deptno on one side so a normal index/PK lookup on dept(deptno, name) can be used instead of scanning/aggregating all 450k dept rows.

The dominant cost is the parallel seq scan of 45M emp rows filtered by ename='A' (estimated ~99 rows). Add a covering index on emp(ename, job, deptno, empno) to enable an index scan; no CTE is needed since the rewritten query is simple and predicate pushdown is direct.
